newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Few road blocks seen for speeding dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Few road blocks seen for speeding dlr/mark.

text.p: After a week of confounding dollar/mark bears, the rate powered through more tough resistance levels on Friday and appears poised for additional gains in the week ahead, chartists said.
"I think trend followers will really pick up on the fact we broke big trendline resistance and that momentum is strong," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at consulting firm I.D.E.A. Inc.
"There's a 100-month moving average at 1.6175, but I think that's probably road-kill," he added, predicting a possible move up to historical congestion levels near 1.6330/50.
By mid-afternoon on Friday dollar/mark had pierced a key 38.2 retracement level -- which technicians pegged at 1.6130/40 -- dating from its highs of June 1989.
Earlier, the rate had barreled through a closely watched 61.8 percent retracement level -- seen at 1.6055/60 -- which dated from its 1994 highs.

"You can talk about these resistance levels but in this kind of market the trend is sharply higher and it's really an issue of using sign posts rather than saying 'this is where I want to sell'," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics. Solin said he was concerned by the swelling number of dollar/mark bulls, which he suggested could be signalling the dollar's move against the mark is nearing an end.

NNNN"You're slowly getting more and more people who, instead of trying to pick tops, are basically throwing the towel in," he said. "That tends to happen toward the end of big moves rather than in the middle of them or at the beginning."
But most chartists warned against picking a top in dollar/mark given its current momentum.
Joseph Klettner, technical foreign exchange analyst at Chase Securities Inc, put the next upside target in dollar/mark at 1.6225, the top of a two-percent trading band.
Barring a near-term stall in the rate and a progression below strong congestion support at around 1.5980, he said further gains to the 1.66 level could be forthcoming.
"I'm a little skeptical about whether we can sustain this move ... but it looks like we're caught up in the euphoria of the stock market," he said.
